key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even when deep defect levels exist, defect-assisted recombination is too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic efficiency losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect engineering likely less critical than in many other materials.
method: First-principles calculations of a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium.
Quantified both radiative and nonradiative Shockley-Read-Hall recombination pathways.
Analyzed how defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping affect recombination rates.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates defect-assisted recombination across many realistic point defects and finds large lattice reorganizations plus energy releases of at least 0.5 E_G per event strongly suppress SRH losses.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on calculated defect kinetics and may still depend on real microstructure, defect concentrations, and device-level transport/recombination conditions.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
